q: How does a project begin?
a: It begins with a conversation, not a quotation. Send your floor plan, a rough budget and the date you need the space by. We reply within one business day with an honest view of whether we are the right studio for it, and if we are, we book a 60-minute consultation — free, in person or on video.

q: Do you charge for the first consultation?
a: No. The first consultation is free and there is no obligation afterwards. We use it to understand the brief, walk the site if it is in Lahore, and give you a budget range. Concept design after that point is a paid stage, because it involves measured surveys and real design time.

q: What information should I send before we meet?
a: Three things help most: an existing floor plan or measured sketch, four to eight images of spaces you like (including one you do not like, which is often more useful), and a target completion date. If you have a society or landlord handbook, send that too — it usually changes the programme.

q: Do you work outside Lahore?
a: Yes. We deliver regularly in Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Faisalabad and Multan, and take on Karachi projects above a certain scale. Outside Lahore we add a mobilisation line to the proposal covering travel, supervision stays and logistics, and we appoint a resident site supervisor rather than commuting the team daily.

q: How is a proposal priced?
a: As a line-item bill of quantities, not a square-foot lump sum. You see each trade, each material and each fixture separately, with quantities taken from the drawings. That is why our budget variance stays under three percent — there is nowhere for an allowance to hide.

q: What is a realistic budget range?
a: For fit-out work in Pakistan, residential typically lands between PKR 1,400 and 2,400 per square foot, commercial between PKR 2,200 and 3,400, and hospitality between PKR 3,000 and 4,200 depending on services and finishes. Design fees are quoted separately and are usually eight to fourteen percent of build cost.

q: What is the payment structure?
a: Commonly 25% on mobilisation, monthly progress payments measured against the programme, and 5% retention released at the end of the defect-liability period. For smaller joinery-only commissions we work to 50% on order and 50% on installation. Everything is written into the contract before work starts.

q: How do you handle variations?
a: Every change is priced and signed before it is built. You receive a one-page variation note showing the cost, the programme impact and the drawing it affects. We do not carry verbal instructions onto site, and we do not present surprise invoices at handover.

q: Can you work to a fixed ceiling budget?
a: Yes, and it is the healthiest way to start. Give us the number you cannot exceed and we design to it — value-engineering materials and scope in that order, never by removing the things that make the space work.

q: How long does a typical project take?
a: Design runs three to six weeks for a home or a small commercial unit, and six to ten weeks for a full floor or restaurant. Construction then runs from four weeks for a single-room renovation to twenty-four weeks for a large turnkey home. We publish the whole programme at contract stage and track it weekly.

q: What are the design stages?
a: Five: measured survey and existing-conditions report, concept and space planning, design development with material and lighting schedules, construction drawings with joinery shop drawings, and 3D visualisation for your approval. You sign off each stage before we move to the next.

q: Do I need to approve 3D visuals before production?
a: For anything we manufacture, yes. The 3D model and the workshop drawings are the same model, so what you approve is what gets cut. It removes almost all of the 'that is not what I pictured' conversation at handover.

q: How often will I hear from you during construction?
a: Every Friday, without fail: a photo report, a one-page progress note against the programme, the decisions we need from you next week, and any risk we can see coming. Plus a WhatsApp thread with your project manager for daily questions.

q: Can I live or work in the space during construction?
a: Often yes. We zone the building, keep one bathroom and one kitchen route live, hoard and sheet daily, and book noisy work inside permitted hours. We will tell you honestly when a six-week move-out is cheaper and less stressful than a twenty-week live build.

q: Do you manufacture in-house?
a: Yes. Our 22,000 sq ft workshop handles panel processing, veneer pressing, spray finishing and metal fabrication with forty-one in-house craftsmen. Nothing is passed to a third-party carpenter who has never seen your drawing, which is the main reason our tolerances hold.

q: What warranty do you provide?
a: Ten years on joinery structure, and a twenty-four-month defect-liability period covering finishes, hardware, services and workmanship. We return at month three and month twelve for a scheduled check, whether or not you call us.

q: Who supervises the site?
a: A dedicated project manager plus a resident site supervisor on every project above PKR 25 lakh. You get their direct number. They own the programme, the daily coordination and the Friday report — and they have authority to stop work if quality or safety is at risk.

q: Do you handle approvals and building management?
a: We do. Society NOCs, building management permits, work-hour bookings, hoarding, insurance, lift protection and the landlord reinstatement list at the end of a lease. For commercial units we also support fire and HVAC approvals through the relevant consultants.

q: What happens at handover?
a: A walkthrough against a room-by-room checklist, a snag list we agree together, an operations and maintenance pack with finishes schedules and warranty certificates, and a two-hour familiarisation session for your team or household. Snags close within fourteen days as standard.

q: Do you take design-only commissions?
a: Yes. We regularly produce drawing and specification packages for clients who build with their own contractor, and we can provide periodic site inspection visits on top. You own the drawings at the end of the engagement.

q: Can you build from another architect's drawings?
a: Frequently. We take the design intent, produce shop drawings and services coordination, and take full responsibility for execution. Where we find something unbuildable we raise it in writing with a proposed alternative rather than improvising on site.

q: Do you supply loose furniture and styling?
a: Yes, as an optional package. We specify, tender across our supplier panel, inspect at the factory, deliver, install and tag assets. For homes we also handle curtains, rugs, art placement and final styling before the handover photographs.

q: Is 3D visualisation available on its own?
a: It is. If you already have drawings, our studio can produce photoreal stills, walkthrough animations or VR-ready scenes from PKR 28,000 per view, typically inside five working days, with two revision rounds included.

q: What is the smallest project you accept?
a: A single bespoke kitchen, wardrobe run or retail counter. Below roughly PKR 15 lakh of build value it usually makes more sense for you to use our design-only package with a local contractor, and we will say so rather than take the job.
